1.title: Recipes and a Team Capstone
1.text: Welcome to Module sixteen: Recipes and a Team Capstone. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Recipes for common mistakes. The team simulation: who does what. Merge, squash, release and hotfix. The final checklist for a team repository. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Course
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the course. Scope: Part six: Practice. Verified with: Git two point five zero.one: every command was run in the lab.

1.title: Recipes for common mistakes
1.text: Recipes for common mistakes. Everybody makes these mistakes, and every one of them has a short fix. The commands come from modules three to seven. The question to ask first is always the same: has the commit left my computer? Before a push you may rewrite. After a push, undo with a new commit.

1.title: Recipes for common mistakes, continued
1.text: Recipes for common mistakes. The figure shows this: Nine common mistakes, each with the short command that fixes it and a warning about when it is safe.

1.title: Recipes for common mistakes, continued
1.text: Recipes for common mistakes. Committed on the wrong branch. Fix: git switch dash c feature slash cart, then git branch dash f main origin slash main. Watch out: Before you push; the commit moves to the new branch. Pushed too early. Fix: git revert head, then git push. Watch out: Adds an undo commit; no force push needed.

1.title: Recipes for common mistakes, continued
1.text: Recipes for common mistakes. Messy history. Fix: git ree base dash i head tilde three, mark the later commits fixup, then git commit the amend flag for the message. Watch out: Only for commits nobody else has. Lost a commit. Fix: git reflog, then git reset the hard flag head at one. Watch out: The reflog lives in your clone only. Wrong commit message. Fix: git commit the amend flag dash m Add login form. Watch out: Only before the push.

1.title: Recipes for common mistakes, continued
1.text: Recipes for common mistakes. Big file committed. Fix: git rm the cached flag big dot bin, add it to dot git ignore, then git commit the amend flag. Watch out: After a push see module fifteen: rotate or rewrite. Detached head. Fix: git switch dash c rescue. Watch out: Do it before you switch away. Merge went wrong. Fix: In conflict: git merge the abort flag. Merged, not pushed: git reset the hard flag orig head. Watch out: orig head is where head was before the merge. Tip: Run git reflog before you panic. It lists where head has been, so a commit lost by a reset is usually one command away.

1.title: Recipes for common mistakes, continued
1.text: Recipes for common mistakes. Pull diverged. Fix: git pull the ree base flag for a straight line, or git pull the no ree base flag for a merge commit. Watch out: A plain git pull stops and asks you to choose. Tip: Use git revert for anything already pushed to a shared branch, and keep reset for commits that only you have. A revert adds history; a reset removes it for you and breaks the clones of everyone else.

1.title: The team simulation: who does what
1.text: The team simulation: who does what. The capstone demonstration plays a whole team in one temporary folder. Nothing is shared except a local bare repository, which stands in for the repository on Git Hub. origin. The bare repository that everybody pushes to and pulls from. Ada. The maintainer: merges the finished branches and tags the releases. Bob. Works on prices; meets a conflict and resolves it on his own branch. Cy. Works on search; later fixes a typo from the release tag.

1.title: The team simulation: who does what, continued
1.text: The team simulation: who does what. Each person starts with a clone and works on a feature branch: feature slash cart, feature slash prices and feature slash search. Ada and Bob both changed the price line of shop dot txt, so the second merge is bound to conflict. The first block shows Ada merging the cart with the no ff flag, which keeps a merge commit as the visible record of the pull request. Then Bob brings origin slash main into his own branch. Your hashes will differ.

1.title: The team simulation: who does what, continued
1.text: The team simulation: who does what. The conflict output belongs to Bob's merge. Bob resolves it on his own branch, so the maintainer's main never sees a broken state. Tip: Resolve a conflict on your own branch: merge the target branch into it, fix the file, then let the maintainer merge a clean branch. Nobody else is blocked while you work.

1.title: Merge, squash, release and hotfix
1.text: Merge, squash, release and hotfix. Ada now merges Bob's branch with the no ff flag and the search branch with the squash flag. A squash merge turns the two search commits into one new commit with a single parent. The original commits stay on the feature branch but not on main. Then Ada tags the release. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Merge, squash, release and hotfix, continued
1.text: Merge, squash, release and hotfix. A bug appears in the release. Cy starts the hotfix from the tag, not from main, because main may hold work that is not released yet. Ada merges the fix and tags it. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Merge, squash, release and hotfix, continued
1.text: Merge, squash, release and hotfix. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Merge, squash, release and hotfix, continued
1.text: Merge, squash, release and hotfix. The lab asserts the shape of this history. The first-parent line of main has five commits, one per unit of work. Three of them are merges, and Bob's conflict resolution makes four merge commits in all. The squash commit has one parent. Both tags are annotated, v one dot zero is an ancestor of v one dot zero dot one, and the three clones end on the same commit as origin. Tip: Branch a hotfix from the release tag, not from main. The fix then contains exactly what you shipped, plus one change.

2.title: The final checklist for a team repository
2.text: The final checklist for a team repository. Start clean. Pull before you start and branch from an up-to-date main. One change, one branch. Give it a short, descriptive name. Commit well. Small commits with a message that says why (module twelve). Use a pull request. Push the branch, open a pull request and link the issue. Wait for green and for a review. Checks and approvals come before the merge (modules nine and eleven). Fix conflicts on your branch. Never settle them with a force push. Leave shared history alone. Rewrite only commits nobody has, and use the force with lease flag, never plain the force flag.

2.title: The final checklist for a team repository, continued
2.text: The final checklist for a team repository. Choose the merge method on purpose. Merge commit, squash or ree base, as the team agreed. Tag releases, hotfix from tags. Annotated tags such as v one dot zero mark what shipped. Keep it safe. No secrets in commits, a protected main, and signed commits if the team asks (module fifteen).

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A wrong commit is already on the shared main that teammates have pulled. What is the safest way to undo it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Run git revert head, then push normally. A revert adds a new commit and rewrites nothing, so the clones of your teammates stay valid.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. A pull ends with "Need to specify how to reconcile divergent branches". What does this output tell you? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Both sides have new commits, so you must choose ree base or merge. The branches diverged, so choose git pull the ree base flag or git pull the no ree base flag.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. You ran git reset the hard flag head tilde one and a day of work disappeared. Nothing was pushed. What brings it back? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: git reflog, then git reset the hard flag head at one. The reflog still lists the lost commit, and resetting to its entry restores it.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. You made two commits on main by mistake and have not pushed. What moves them to a new branch and cleans main? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: git switch dash c feature slash cart, then git branch dash f main origin slash main. The new branch keeps the commits, and moving main back to origin slash main removes them from it.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Cy's branch has two commits, and Ada squash merges it into main. What does main show afterwards? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: One new commit with one parent, and no trace of the two. A squash merge creates a single new commit, and the original commits stay on the feature branch only.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. v one dot zero shipped last week and main holds newer unreleased work. A bug needs a quick fix for production. Where should the hotfix branch start? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: From the v one dot zero tag, which is exactly what shipped. A hotfix from the release tag contains only the shipped code plus the one fix.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which command undoes a pushed commit without rewriting history? Answer: git revert. Question two. Which command lists where head has been, to find a lost commit? Answer: git reflog. Question three. What does git merge the abort flag do? Answer: It stops a conflicted merge and restores the branch to the state before it.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which merge option forces a merge commit even when a fast-forward is possible? Answer: the no ff flag. Question five. How do you create an annotated tag for a release? Answer: git tag dash a v one dot zero dash m Release one dot zero. Question six. Which push option is safer than the force flag? Answer: the force with lease flag.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. First question: has the commit left my computer? Not pushed: rewrite. Pushed: revert. Wrong branch: git switch dash c feature slash cart, then git branch dash f main origin slash main. Lost or wrong: git reflog and git reset the hard flag head at one; git commit the amend flag; git switch dash c rescue for a detached head. Merge trouble: git merge the abort flag in conflict; git reset the hard flag orig head after an unpushed merge. Diverged pull: git pull the ree base flag for a line, git pull the no ree base flag for a merge commit. Merge styles: the no ff flag keeps a merge commit; the squash flag makes one single-parent commit. Release and hotfix: git tag dash a v one dot zero; hotfix branch from the tag; tag the fix v one dot zero dot one.
